subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Which subset of canonical readiness conditions, standard and operator profiles, plugin callbacks, activation identity, and release-conformance obligations should OpenClaw accept now?
rationale: The proposal and exact-head proof establish feasibility, but only maintainers can choose the permanent core API, failure policy, compatibility boundary, and release support promise.

options.title: Accept the proven foundation
options.body: Approve canonical conditions, legacy compatibility projections, and the proven initial profile and provider surfaces while deferring activation identity and blocking release gates.

options.title: Accept the complete roadmap
options.body: Approve the full RFC, including presently unimplemented activation and release-support obligations, as one long-term contract.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Keep hosting-readiness composition host- or plugin-owned rather than establishing this core support contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the proven foundation
recommendation.body: Approve canonical conditions, legacy compatibility projections, and the proven initial profile and provider surfaces while deferring activation identity and blocking release gates.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the repository's acceptance lifecycle and are the strongest evidence-backed routing candidate for advancing this draft through formal RFC direction.
